reconcile.note: Adam Clarke concedes Samuel was no priest and sacrificed away from the tabernacle, but grounds it in necessity since neither tabernacle nor ark was then at hand.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen dismisses the Mizpah narrative as a late pious fiction in which Samuel, no priest, sacrifices apart from any sanctioned altar.

quotes.text: Samuel, however, sacrifices a sucking lamb and cries for help to Jehovah, and the engagement takes place while he is so occupied.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), ch. VII, on 1 Samuel 7:9.

sides.snippet: that man shall be cut off from among his people.
sides.verseText: and hasn't brought it to the door of the Tent of Meeting, to offer it as an offering to Yahweh before the tabernacle of Yahweh: blood shall be imputed to that man. He has shed blood; and that man shall be cut off from among his people.

sides.snippet: Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt-offering to Yahweh
sides.verseText: Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt-offering to Yahweh: and Samuel cried to Yahweh for Israel; and Yahweh answered him.
